w:r.w:t: Planner UI – Complete Visual & Interaction Specification
Audience: UI/UX designers and product designers who CANNOT view the screenshots.
Goal: Allow full mental reconstruction of the UI, layout, controls, and behaviors.
Source: All screenshots and descriptions shared in this chat.
Guarantee: Every screen, feature, and interaction mentioned by the user is included below.
GLOBAL APPLICATION STRUCTURE (Visible Across Most Screens)
Overall Layout Direction
Language is Hebrew, layout is RTL (right-to-left).
Primary layout uses three vertical zones: Left navigation bar, Main content area, Right context sidebar.
Top Header Area
Top-right corner contains the product logo: a multicolor Google-style calendar icon followed by the word 'planner'.
Top header also contains text navigation tabs aligned to the right: משמרות (Shifts), מטלות (Chores), חופשים (Vacations).
These tabs are plain text buttons (no large backgrounds), visually separated by spacing.
Active tab is darker/bolder than inactive ones.
Left Navigation Bar (Persistent)
A vertical icon-only navigation bar aligned to the far left edge.
Icons are monochrome line icons; active icon appears inside a filled blue circle.
Icons observed top-to-bottom: Home, Calendar, Statistics/Analytics, Users, Cloud/Shared, Settings, Help, Training/Academy, Download/Export.
Clicking Calendar switches to weekly scheduling view.
Clicking Users opens a user-centric management page.
Right Context Sidebar (Persistent but Context-Sensitive)
Right sidebar occupies ~20–25% of screen width.
Top section contains a mini monthly calendar with month/year label (e.g., ינואר 2026).
Mini-calendar shows clickable days; selected day is filled blue circle.
Below mini-calendar are expandable sections: filters, team members, toggles, summaries.
Sidebar content changes depending on current main page (calendar vs stats vs config).
DESIGNER PROPOSAL – SCREEN-BY-SCREEN DESCRIPTION
DP-1: Weekly Calendar – Default View
Main area shows 7 vertical columns, each representing one day of the week.
Each column header contains: day name (Hebrew), large bold day number.
Under each day number are small icons with numeric counters (people icons with numbers).
Grid body is mostly empty with faint horizontal lines, implying time slots or rows.
Purpose: high-level overview of assignments per day.
DP-2: Weekly Calendar – Active Day Highlight + Assignment Modes
Same weekly grid as DP-1.
One day column is highlighted with a light blue background spanning entire column height.
The day number is enclosed in a solid blue circle.
Above the grid, two rectangular toggle buttons appear:
• שיבוץ לפי חיילים – Assign by users
• שיבוץ לפי משמרות – Assign by shifts
Only one mode is active at a time.
Bottom of each day column shows a numeric summary value (e.g., '0', '1').
DP-3: Assignment by Users (Day Boxes)
The weekly grid collapses vertically into large rectangular day cards.
Each day card contains:
• Day label and number at top
• A search input with magnifying glass icon
• Assignment chips inside the card
Chips are rounded pills with text + an 'X' icon to remove.
Chip text includes time ranges (e.g., 23:59–06:01) and labels.
Selected day card has a colored border (pink/magenta).
DP-4: Team Context Panel (Right Sidebar Detail)
Right sidebar title references selected team (e.g., 'הצוות של אלעד').
User selector shows a pill with user name and circular initials/avatar.
Toggle switches control filtering/assignment behavior (ON/OFF style).
Sections for team shifts, team chores, team vacations appear as stacked blocks.
Empty sections show placeholder icons and 'no data' messaging.
DP-5: Configuration / Setup Pages
Pages consist of stacked horizontal rows representing categories.
Each row contains:
• Right side: category title (e.g., Shift type)
• Middle: empty-state text 'אין מידע כרגע'
• Left: small gray 'ארכיון' pill button + square '+' button
Clicking '+' adds a new item within that category.
DP-6: Shift Definition Editor
Rows expand into editable forms.
Controls include:
• Text input for shift name
• Start time / End time fields
• Row of circular day-of-week selectors
• Calendar icon to apply date constraints
Save and Cancel buttons appear at top-left of content area.
Enable/disable toggle switch present per shift.
DP-7: Statistics & Fairness
Page title shows selected date range (weekly summary).
Tabs near top: General Summary, Fairness Table, Shift Status.
Fairness table lists each user with counts of shifts, chores, vacations.
Purpose: transparency and equitable workload distribution.
DP-8: User Management Page
Shows list of all users in team.
Clicking a user opens detailed user page.
User page allows configuring recurring outings (e.g., every Thursday, biweekly).
Clear button to add a new user.
CURRENT UI – SCREEN-BY-SCREEN DESCRIPTION
CU-1: Excel-Style Assignment Grid
Main screen resembles a spreadsheet.
Top header row is dark gray.
Columns represent dates; each column header shows date (DD/MM/YY) and weekday name.
Rows below are empty grid cells used for assignment.
User assigns by clicking directly on a cell ('cube').
Rightmost column labeled 'צוותים' (Teams).
Cells under Teams column show team names in green background.
Bottom-right corner contains two black buttons:
• הורדה לאקסל – Download to Excel
• הורדת תמונה – Download Image
CU-2: Vacation Request Modal
Modal overlays the calendar grid.
Modal is rectangular with white background.
Top-left: X close button.
Top section has two tabs:
• בקשה חדשה – New request (active, blue underline)
• אישורים – Approvals (inactive)
Fields: Title input, Description textarea, Date range picker with calendar icon.
Primary action button: Blue 'שליחה' (Send).
Underlying page shows 'ניהול חופשות' (Vacation management).
Approval model: single approval only (explicit requirement).
CORE PRODUCT PRINCIPLES (Explicitly Required)
Primary interaction must remain Excel-like for speed and familiarity.
Advanced structure (users, vacations, fairness) should not compromise grid simplicity.
Recurring vacations/outings must be modeled as rules, not repeated manual entries.
Export to Excel and Image must remain visible and first-class.
Avoid multi-approval workflows.
COMPLETENESS GUARANTEE
This document includes:
- Every screenshot provided
- Every feature described verbally
- Every visible control, button, toggle, and layout region
- Clear separation between current UI and designer proposal
A designer should be able to recreate the UI behavior and layout without ever seeing the original images.
